figures.caption: Figure 1: Resolved parameter-space flows for the wedge-trained classifier. (a) The equivariance-directed flow along b⋆ moves the realised function towards the equivariant subspace, reducing its non-invariant component. (b) The symmetrydirected flow along c⋆ moves the realised function along its rotational symmetry orbit while approximately preserving its distance from the equivariant subspace. The local direction is recomputed at every integration step.

Figure 2: Global and infinitesimal lifting through the neural-network realisation map. Left: can a symmetry transformation in function space be realised by a transformation in parameter space? Right: do the infinitesimal symmetry directions lie in the function-space tangent directions accessible through the parametrisation?

Figure 3: Angular deviation profiles for the ASRNN trained to model the Mexican hat potential for various values of α unseen during training. Top: symmetry-directed flow along c⋆. Bottom: equivariance-directed flow along b⋆. Here the local direction is recomputed at every step, i.e. the Resolved trajectory.

Figure 4: Angular deviation profiles for the ASRNN trained to model the Mexican hat potential for various values of α unseen during training. Top: symmetry-directed flow along c⋆. Bottom: equivariance-directed flow along b⋆. Here the direction is computed once at t = 0 and kept fixed, i.e. the Fixed trajectory.

Figure 5: Fixed parameter-space flows across training conditions. (a) Angular deviation profiles along the symmetry- and equivariance-directed flows. (b) Decision boundaries along the symmetry-directed flow c⋆. (c) Decision boundaries along the equivariance-directed flow b⋆. The parameter-space directions are computed once at t = 0 and kept fixed throughout the trajectory.

Figure 6: Resolved parameter-space flows across training conditions. (a) Angular deviation profiles along the symmetry- and equivariance-directed flows. (b) Decision boundaries along the symmetry-directed flow c⋆. (c) Decision boundaries along the equivariance-directed flow b⋆. The Jacobian and corresponding parameterspace directions are recomputed at every step.

Figure 8: Fixed parameter-space flows for the wedge-trained classifier. (a) The initial equivariance-directed direction b⋆ does not continue to move the realised function towards the equivariant subspace. (b) The initial symmetry-directed direction c⋆ deviates from the intended rotational symmetry orbit. In both cases, the direction is computed once at t = 0 and kept fixed throughout the trajectory.
